About Gulfport

Living in Gulfport

Gulfport is the largest city on the Mississippi Gulf Coast and shares the job of Harrison County seat with Biloxi. It was founded at the end of the 1800s as a railroad and shipping town, and the Port of Gulfport is still a big part of the local economy.

Homes range from older cottages and bungalows near downtown and the beach to newer subdivisions north of Interstate 10. The city covers a lot of ground, so it is worth narrowing a search by ZIP code and commute.

Places to know

Around Gulfport

  • Jones Park and the Gulfport harborWaterfront park, marina and event space where US 90 meets US 49.
  • Mississippi AquariumDowntown aquarium with indoor and outdoor exhibits, opened in 2020.
  • Ship Island excursionsSeasonal ferry from the Gulfport harbor to West Ship Island in Gulf Islands National Seashore.
  • Downtown GulfportRestaurants, bars and shops a few blocks from the beach.
  • Gulfport-Biloxi International AirportThe Coast's main commercial airport, inside Gulfport city limits.
  • Gulfport Premium OutletsOutlet shopping at Interstate 10 and US 49.

Getting around

Roads and commute

US 90 runs along the beach, Interstate 10 crosses the north side of the city, and US 49 heads north toward Hattiesburg. The Naval Construction Battalion Center (the Seabee base) is in Gulfport, and Keesler Air Force Base in Biloxi is a short drive east.

Workers who live in Gulfport spend an average of 21.9 minutes getting to work, one way (Mississippi average: 25.6).

Near the water

Flood zones and insurance costs can change from one street to the next on the Coast. Look up any address on FEMA's flood map, and ask me for help getting insurance quotes before you make an offer.
